name: Jump rope smoothly
blurb: Cheap, portable and brutally effective conditioning. Smooth skipping is about small wrist circles and low, quiet jumps rather than athleticism.
gear: A rope sized so the handles reach your armpits when you stand on the middle
steps: Size the rope and start with no rope: practise a low bounce on the balls of your feet, barely leaving the floor.
Practise turning the rope with your wrists only, elbows in at your sides.
Combine: one jump per turn, aiming for a quiet landing.
Build to unbroken sets — 30 seconds, then a minute, then three.
Learn to relax. Smooth skipping is much less tiring than tense skipping.
Add intervals: 30 seconds hard, 30 easy, ten rounds.
tips: Jumping too high is the main fault. Two centimetres of clearance is plenty.
Whipped shins mean the rope is too long or your arms are drifting out.
proof: Three unbroken minutes at a steady rhythm without a trip.
